title: Hysteresis arbiter for prefix-sliced LRU+TTL eviction under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Kline
description:
Goal: design and implement an eviction "arbiter" that combines LRU and TTL signals with prefix-aware slicing and operational hysteresis so the KV cache behaves correctly and predictably under continuous batching and volatile GPU memory pressure. The arbiter must provide clear correctness guarantees (no active-batch eviction, bounded staleness per-prefix, deterministic fences for invalidation) while optimizing for reuse (hit-rate) and overall GPU memory efficiency.

Background/context: Continuous batching increases temporal overlap of requests touching many prefixes in short windows. Naive LRU can thrash when batches touch many prefixes; TTL-only policies leave long-tail prefixes occupying expensive GPU slab memory. Prefix-aware eviction reduces cross-prefix interference but introduces complexity around atomic invalidation and correctness when prefix entries are pinned by in-flight batches. We need: 1) a hybrid LRU+TTL scoring function, 2) per-prefix slice accounting and reservation windows, 3) hysteresis to prevent eviction oscillation during bursts, 4) a lease/fencing mechanism to prevent in-use entries from being evicted mid-batch, 5) GPU-slab-aware compaction hooks to avoid fragmentation.

Non-goals: We will not change the network routing or batching algorithm itself in this ticket. This is solely cache eviction policy and correctness scaffolding; performance micro-optimizations to kernel-level memory copies will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and accepted by runtime and infra leads (link in attachments)
Hybrid scoring implemented: entries score computed from recency (LRU decaying counter), TTL bias, and per-prefix hotness; documented formula and constants
Lease/fence mechanism prevents eviction of entries touched by any active batch; failing test coverage if eviction attempt while lease active
Per-prefix bounded-staleness invariant: prefix entries not accessed for N_ms (configurable) become reclaimable; verified by property tests and fuzz runs
Hysteresis (two thresholds: soft reclaim and hard reclaim) implemented per GPU shard and prevents oscillation under synthetic burst workloads (seen in perf dashboards)
GPU memory fragmentation reduced (tracked via slab free ratio) compared to baseline in A/B perf tests run for 24h
Automated regression suite (unit + integration + stress) added and run in CI with deterministic seeds
Canary rollout plan executed (shadow -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback on >5% latency or >3% reduction in hit-rate
Documentation (runtime handbook + console doc) added describing operational knobs and SLO impact
tasks: Draft design doc: describe data structures, scoring formula, lease TTLs, hysteresis thresholds, invariants and failure modes
Implement per-prefix slice accounting (in-memory counters, reservation windows)
Add LRU-decay + TTL bias scoring module and tie to background reclaim worker
Implement lease/fence API used by batching runtime to pin entries during active use
Integrate GPU-slab compaction hooks so reclamation can coalesce freed slabs
Add property-based tests and fuzz harness that simulates continuous batching patterns (multi-prefix, variable sequence lengths)
Run 24h A/B perf job against synthetic and small production trace, gather dashboard metrics
Prepare rollout flags and canary pipeline, add observability (per-prefix hit-rate, eviction-reasons, lease-block-count)
Write docs and run a short knowledge share with SE/Support teams
comments: 2025-11-05 - Aisha Kline: Kickoff meeting notes added. Consensus: prefer hybrid scoring over pure LRU for tail workloads. Action: Marco to prototype scoring in a feature branch.

2025-12-12 - Marco Duarte: Prototype commit available in https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4182 — contains scoring stub and per-prefix counters. Initial microbench shows +6% hit-rate on synthetic prefix-skew workload.

2026-01-08 - Priya Nair (infra review): Suggested adding explicit lease sequence numbers to handle overlapping batch cancellations. Raised concern about race if background worker sees lease expired but batch still holds GPU pointer; recommended short 'grace' fence and validation epoch.

2026-01-22 - Marco Duarte: Implemented lease epoch and grace fence; added unit test that emulates batch cancellation and ensures eviction is blocked until fence resolution. Tests added in runtime/test/lease_fence_test.go

2026-02-10 - QA: Stress run (12h) with wide-batch workload surfaced oscillation when hysteresis thresholds too tight. Re-tuned soft/hard thresholds and re-ran. Oscillation eliminated in 6h run; metrics attached.
2026-03-02 - Security review request: submitted. Note: design does not add new network surfaces; KMS/HSM unaffected. Awaiting formal confirmation.

2026-03-10 - Marco Duarte: Preparing canary config (feature flag runtime.eviction.hysteresis=true). Next step: shadow for 48h on non-customer clusters then 10% canary. See rollout checklist in attachments.
